claims.claim: Both Smith and Marx shared a contempt for unproductive labor and menial servants who leave nothing behind in return for their consumption.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Moreover, both Smith and Marx were in agreement with modern public opinion when they despised unproductive labor as parasitical, actually a kind of perversion of labor, as though nothing were worthy of this name which did not enrich the world. Marx certainly shared Smith’s contempt for the “menial servants” who like “idle guests . . . leave nothing behind them in return for their consumption.”

claims.claim: Marx's introduction of the term labor power (Arbeitskraft) was considered by Engels to be the most original and revolutionary element of his entire system.
claims.supporting_excerpt: It is because not labor itself but the surplus of human “labor power ” ( Arbeits kraft) explains labor’s productivity that Marx’s introduction of this term, as Engels rightly remarked, constituted the most original and revolutionary element of his whole system.

definitions.definition: A human power whose strength is not exhausted by producing the means of its own subsistence and survival, but is capable of producing a surplus beyond what is necessary for its own reproduction.

distinctions.distinction: The productivity of work adds new objects to the human artifice, whereas the productivity of labor power produces objects only incidentally, is primarily concerned with the means of its own reproduction, and never produces anything but life.

must_not_be_lost: The distinction between productive and unproductive labor conceals the more fundamental distinction between work and labor.
Under a completely socialized mankind focused entirely on the life process, the distinction between labor and work would completely disappear as all things become functions of the life process.
parsed.segment_function: Analyze the historical and theoretical conflation of productive labor, unproductive labor, work, and labor power in modern economic theory, particularly through the views of Smith and Marx.
